summary: Gives replacement text and a replacement figure for the Very Distant Host specification in BBN Report 1822, which defined how a Host connects to an IMP. Readers were asked to file it with their copy of Report 1822 until that document was next updated.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC provides replacement text and a control-word figure for the Very Distant Host specification. It explains how an IMP and Host detect a failed line and attempt to restore it.

questions: how do you know if an imp connection is dead
subtitle: A revised control-word diagram and liveness procedure for very distant Hosts.

tldr.problem: The Very Distant Host specification in BBN Report 1822 needed replacement text and a control-word figure.
tldr.mechanism: The replacement procedure uses periodic HELLO packets and I-HEARD-YOU acknowledgements to decide whether a line is alive.
tldr.outcome: The RFC asks readers to keep the replacement material with their copy of Report 1822 until its update.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 547's status as Unknown. The RFC supplies replacement material for BBN Report 1822.

sections.title: Replacement Figure for the Control Word
sections.content:
RFC 547 supplies a new version of Figure F-4 and replacement text for the Very Distant Host section of BBN Report 1822. The figure labels control-word fields including packet count, channel number, acknowledgements, HELLO/I-HEARD-YOU, and special packet bits.

The author asks readers to place the RFC with their copy of Report 1822 pending its update.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC replaces one control-word figure and its accompanying text in Report 1822. The diagram labels fields used in Host-IMP communication.

sections.title: Testing Whether the Line Is Alive
sections.content:
Both the IMP and Host send a HELLO special packet every r seconds. When either side receives a HELLO, it promptly returns an I-HEARD-YOU packet; if a side sends more than t HELLO packets without an acknowledgement, it declares the line dead.

After the dead-line waiting period, a side sends HELLO packets until k in a row are acknowledged. Then it declares the line alive and regular packets can again be exchanged.
sections.plainLanguage: Each side sends HELLO and expects I-HEARD-YOU in reply. Repeated missed acknowledgements mark the line dead; a run of acknowledged HELLO packets marks it alive again.

sections.title: Timing Values and Reset Behavior
sections.content:
The RFC gives current values of r as 1.25 seconds, t as 4, and k as 4. It advises implementers to make these parameters easy to change because they may be adjusted later.

When a line is declared dead, the odd/even bits, used/unused bits, and channel filling and emptying sequences are to be reinitialized.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC gives the current values for the HELLO interval and retry thresholds. It says to make them easy to change and to reinitialize channel state after a dead line.
